instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Insurance brokerage firm advising corporate clients on risk management programs spanning property, casualty, cyber, D&O, and employee benefits. Team of 35 brokers managing €60M in placed premiums. Seeking to implement a risk analytics platform for client exposure modeling and benchmarking. We operate across multiple geographies and business units with a matrix organizational structure. A centralized digital transformation office coordinates innovation initiatives, but business unit autonomy means adoption varies significantly. Annual capex budget for innovation exists but deployment is gated by rigorous ROI modeling and steering committee approval.
answers.pastInitiatives: A junior engineer built an internal dashboard to visualize our order backlog, which the operations team found useful. However, this was an informal side project with no official support or maintenance plan. When that engineer left, the dashboard became unreliable and was eventually abandoned. We learned that good ideas need institutional backing to survive.
answers.strategicGoals: We are targeting a 20% improvement in operational throughput without increasing headcount. Our processes have grown organically over the years and are overdue for standardization. We suspect that workflow digitization, basic automation, and better data integration between our core systems can unlock significant productivity gains within our current cost structure.

input.changes_since_last: Completed 3 strategic partnerships. Revenue growth 5% YoY. Exploring AI/ML capabilities.

opportunities.title: Enterprise Workflow Standardization and Automation Framework
opportunities.rationale: The core strategic goal is 20% operational throughput improvement, which requires tackling the current 'organic' process structure. Establishing a standardized framework minimizes risk and maximizes ROI by automating repeatable tasks in high-volume business units.

first_actions: Form a cross-functional Process Owner group to map 3 priority end-to-end processes (e.g., claim intake, policy renewal).
Select and pilot low-code/no-code RPA tools for the least complex standardization opportunity.
Define clear governance rules for process change management that must be approved by business unit leads.
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in average cycle time for the 3 mapped processes by X%
milestones: Completion of 'As-Is' state mapping for Process A.
Pilot automation successful with measurable cost/time savings achieved.
Formalized process governance charter adopted by the committee.

opportunities.title: Centralized Risk Data Lake and Predictive Modeling Pilot
opportunities.rationale: To shift from reactive risk advice to predictive modeling, Nexus needs a single source of truth. Starting with a pilot data lake connecting core systems will provide the necessary structure for AI/ML exploration while keeping the scope contained and manageable.

first_actions: Identify 3 key, discrete data sets (e.g., claim history, client demographics, market indices) for initial integration.
Define strict data governance protocols to ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements before ingestion.
Secure commitment from IT and Business Intelligence teams to allocate time for ETL development.
resources_needed: Cloud Data Warehouse/Lake resources (e.g., Snowflake, Azure Synapse)
execution_plan.success_metric: Successful ingestion and queryability of 3 core data sets for joint analysis.
milestones: Data governance framework documented and approved.
Minimum Viable Data Lake established with validated connections.
Delivery of the first predictive dashboard prototype (e.g., claim frequency predictor).

next_steps.action: Establish a dedicated Process Standardization Working Group with clear charters and mandated attendance from key business units to drive process mapping.
Conduct a comprehensive data lineage and gap analysis across core systems to identify the highest-value, lowest-effort points for initial integration into the Data Lake.
Identify one single, high-volume operational task (e.g., manual data entry into client policy files) suitable for immediate RPA piloting to build internal capability and demonstrate quick wins.

key_weaknesses: Siloed systems prevent holistic risk views, creating manual data gaps.
Organizational processes are highly ad-hoc and lack formalized ownership or standardized documentation (Process Barrier).
Decision-making structure is effective but risks slowing down execution due to overly rigorous ROI modeling gates.

improvements: Increased investment capacity: Budget allocated increased from 3% to 8% of capex.
Validated external partnerships (3 strategic partnerships) which expand operational scope and market reach.
Goal clarity established: Defined target of 20% operational throughput improvement drives focus.
persistent_gaps: Lack of centralized, standardized process mapping requires manual effort that is prone to failure.
Data integration remains tactical rather than strategic, limiting predictive capability.
Organizational talent needs upskilling in automation and data governance best practices.
achieved_milestones: Formalization of innovation initiatives: Moves from 'informal' side projects to committee-governed programs.
Completion of previous opportunity (opp_3) provides institutional credibility for future funding rounds.

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The focus has shifted from merely identifying opportunities to defining concrete execution paths and gaining budgetary commitment. The move from 'informal' awareness to a structured framework is evident, particularly concerning the prioritization of efficiency gains.
